steps.title: Assemble the rack
steps.text: Build the StarTech 4POSTRACK42 (42U), set the rail-to-rail depth to 900 mm and level it. Make it stable before anything heavy goes in: lower the levelling feet until the castors are off the floor (or lock every castor) and fit the rack's stabiliser or floor anchor if one is supplied. Fit the rack earth bar (RACK-EARTH, grounding kit) on the left rear post with paint-piercing washers; it is bonded to the lab earth bar in the next step, before anything else goes in. Stack from U1 upwards, power at the bottom. Fit the M6 cage nuts with the cage-nut tool as each item goes in: 4 per front- or rear-mounted item, 84 for the items plus 2 per rear lacing bar (94 in all; front or rear posts as each step says; rail-kit servers, the UNIRAILS1U rails (own M5 hardware) and blanking panels need none).

steps.title: Cable: Earth bond
steps.text: Bond the rack earth bar (RACK-EARTH, left rear post) to the lab earth bar with B001: 6 mm2 green/yellow, 2-hole lug with paint-piercing washers at the rack bar, ring lug at the lab bar; crimp the lugs with the ring-lug crimper and torque them with the torque wrench to the value marked on each stud. Print two ID labels and tag both ends. Check it end to end with the multimeter on ohms, test leads nulled first (REL): under 0.1 ohm. From now on wear the ESD strap bonded to this earth.

steps.title: Mount the PDUs
steps.text: Fit the 2 switched PDUs at U1-U2 (1U each) on the REAR posts (4 cage nuts + screws each, at the rear), outlets and network port facing the rear. Commission each PDU bare, before any lead is fitted: plug its cord into its wall socket with nothing connected, enable front-panel outlet switching, set every outlet OFF and every outlet's power-on state to OFF (front panel or local port), check on its display that every outlet reads OFF, set its management address, then unplug the cord again. From here on the PDU cords stay out of the wall until power-up.

steps.title: Mount the DC drawers
steps.text: Rectifier shelves and distribution panels above the PDUs, on the front posts (ears on 4 cage nuts + screws each); the two rectifier shelves also run on a pair of UNIRAILS1U rails, bolted to the front and rear posts with the rail kit's own M5 cage nuts and screws. DC-RECT2 (U3) and DC-DIST2 (U4) give -48 V to the IP-50 radios; the DC-DIST2 RTN bus (= DC-RECT2 +V) is bonded to the rack earth bar (B002, first item of the DC cable step), which makes the -48 V system positive grounded, and bus B is strapped to bus A (D016). DC-RECT (U5) and DC-DIST (U6) give +48 V to the node adaptors and the Spider-box DCIN inputs; DC-RECT's output stays floating (not earthed). Every breaker (5 A or less) OFF, the DCD1M main / input breaker too if the panel has one; every GMT fuse OUT, bagged and labelled with its position until power-up. Label the fronts with the label printer: DC-RECT and DC-DIST '+48 V FLOATING - NODES', DC-RECT2 and DC-DIST2 '-48 V POSITIVE GROUND - IP-50': the two rectifier shelves are the same part, so the label is what tells them apart.

steps.title: Adaptor shelf
steps.text: Fit the 1U shelf at U7 on the front posts (4 cage nuts). Positions are measured from the left ear as seen from the FRONT (your right-hand ear when you stand at the rear). Rear row, left to right: PA-01 (node B), PA-02 (node E), PA-03 (node H), PA-04 (node A), PA-05 (node D), PA-06 (node C), PA-07 (node F); front row, at the far right, unwired spares PA-08 to PA-10. RJ45 and DC terminals face the rear; every body 15 mm or more from the next.

steps.title: Programmable attenuators
steps.text: Fit one 1U vented shelf (front posts, 4 cage nuts) at the bottom of each 2U attenuator space and stand its one or two attenuator boxes on it, ATT-01 top-left, numbers increasing left to right and downwards. SMA IN/OUT and the dial face the front; LAN and power at the back. Each box's plug-in power adapter is Velcroed to the rear lacing bar beside its shelf, never on the shelf between the boxes.

steps.title: Coupler tray (16 couplers)
steps.text: Fit the 1U shelf at the bottom of the 3U space U18-U20 (front posts, 4 cage nuts); leave the upper 2U open. Lay the 16 couplers flat, all the same way round: IN on the LEFT end (toward the Spider tile), THRU on the RIGHT end (toward the link attenuator), CPL on top (toward the arm attenuator). Two columns, rows front to back = tile 1-4 of each group: left column CPL-BE, CPL-AS; right column CPL-DW, CPL-EN. The DC blocks and pads that stand on the CPL ports (ARM-*) go on in the coupling-arm steps: up to 52 mm, then the plug and the cable bend; the arm cable runs level 95 mm above the port, 19 mm under the unit above. Cable lanes so no rear-row cable runs through a front-row plug: IN and THRU cables leave 18 mm straight out, then each row further back moves 6 mm further out before running forward; the arm cables move 12 mm to the right of their stack, plus 6 mm per row, and run forward side by side.

steps.title: Spider boxes
steps.text: Mount the four 1U Spider boxes SB1 (top, U24) to SB4 (U21). Which box goes where: SB1 = GTS003 #1, serial SF06000007 (assumed); SB2 = GTST002B, serial SF06000001; SB3 = GTST003, serial SF06000058; SB4 = GTS003 #2, serial SF06000031 (assumed). Check the serial on each box's label before it goes in. For each box fit a pair of UNIRAILS1U rails first, bolted to the front AND rear posts with the M5 cage nuts and screws in the rail kit; slide the box onto them and fix its ears on 4 M6 cage nuts + screws at the front. Odd / even / hybrid is the Terragraph polarity the E2E controller gives each node (a software setting, not a label on the box): the same box can be odd in one PoC and even in the next. The module map of each front panel is in the close-ups that follow the table of this step. Hold point before any DCIN run is landed at its box: confirm what the green DC terminal block (DCIN) on each box's rear feeds and at what voltage. The design assumes the box fans and the Raspberry Pi at 48 V DC, fed from DC-DIST CB8-CB10 (D017-D020, SB1 on CB8; SB2 on CB9; SB3 on CB10; SB4 on CB10), landed at power-up only. Any other voltage or function: STOP; the DCIN runs stay unlanded and the design changes; if DCIN turns out to feed a node, that node's power path changes.

steps.title: Servers and traffic hosts
steps.text: Fit the rail kits shipped with each server (toolless in square holes) and slide the servers in one at a time, network ports at the back (sizes in the rack schedule). Never have more than one server pulled out on its rails at a time: the rack can tip.

steps.title: Switches, cable manager
steps.text: Cable manager at U25 (front posts), between HOST-E above and SB1 below; SW-DATA at U35 on the front posts, ports to the front, on a pair of UNIRAILS1U rails (front and rear posts, kit M5 hardware; Netgear's RBS1830 fits 18-30 in rails only); SW-OOB at U34 on the REAR posts, ports to the rear; GNSS splitter at U36, connectors to the rear. Then fit 5 lacing bars on the rear posts (2 cage nuts each), power on the left and data on the right as seen from the front.

steps.title: Blanking panels
steps.text: Blank every empty U (toolless panels, no cage nuts).

steps.title: Bench table
steps.text: Place the bench table to the right of the rack and fit the cable bridge (CABLE-BRIDGE) from the rack's right post to the table's rack-side end, its floor at table height, divider in: data in the front compartment, power in the rear one. Set out the equipment at the positions in the table (every item 5 mm or more from the next): the operator station nearest the rack (keyboard at the front, monitor behind it, BENCH-CTL behind the monitor) and the strip lengthwise just right of the monitor (610 mm from the rack-side end), inlet toward the back edge; MWATT in the middle, 90 mm in from the front edge, with the IP-50 radios left (A side) and right (B side) of it in a front and a back row 120 mm apart, waveguide flanges toward MWATT; stacked radios sit on two 25 mm spacer bars on the lid of the one below (front and rear edge), each bar fixed to the lower lid with double-sided foam tape and the upper radio pressed onto tape on the bars so it cannot slide: IP50-MCD@C on IP50-MAF@A, IP50-MCD@D on IP50-MAF@F; the analyser at the far end; screw the table earth bar (TABLE-EARTH) to the table's back edge behind MWATT, studs up just below the top. Keep the back 110 mm of the table clear for the cable lanes: data bundle 70-110 mm from the back edge, power bundle within 30 mm of it; keep the aisle between the strip and the A-side radios clear.

steps.title: Cable: DC power and earth bonds
steps.text: 28 cables; print two ID labels per cable on the label printer and tag both ends before routing. First the earth bonds and the -48 V system's own wiring, all made before any feed is landed: bond the DC-DIST2 RTN bus earth stud to the rack earth bar with B002 (6 mm2 green/yellow: positive ground); strap bus B to bus A with D016 (skip the strap if the panel ships strapped); bond the table earth bar to the rack earth bar with B004 (6 mm2, along the floor under the cable protector with the strip cord) and each IP-50 radio's chassis ground screw to its TABLE-EARTH stud with B005-B010 (2.5 mm2 green/yellow; ground screw position TBC); crimp the lugs with the ring-lug crimper, torque them with the torque wrench to the value marked on each stud, and check every bond end to end with the multimeter (leads nulled, under 0.1 ohm). Strip each end with the wire stripper and ferrule every stranded end (ferrule crimper). Conductor convention: before landing a run, shrink a red (+48 V) or blue (-48 V) sleeve onto the SUPPLY conductor at both ends with the heat gun (breaker or fuse output, or supply terminal); the unsleeved conductor is the 0 V return. Land each run at its breaker, fuse or supply end only and torque those terminals to the value marked on them (DCD1M, N250110) with the torque screwdriver; leave the LOAD end (adaptor DC terminal, Spider DCIN terminal, radio DC plug) unlanded, tagged and taped with insulating tape: it is landed and torqued at the polarity check at power-up. The Spider DCIN runs (D017-D020, box fans / Pi) are landed at their breakers like the others; their box end stays unlanded until the hold point of step 8 has confirmed DCIN is a 48 V DC input. CB10 takes two runs (D019, D020): both supply conductors in one twin ferrule. Rack runs go up the LEFT side of the rack as seen from the front (your right-hand side when you stand at the rear), on the rear lacing bars, 50 mm or more from coax and data. The IP-50 feeds are the exception: from DC-DIST2's front fuse outputs they run along the front of its U to the RIGHT side of the rack, back to about 640 mm behind the front rail and up to table height in their own wrapped power bundle, then cross in the REAR (power) compartment of the cable bridge. On the table every radio feed runs in the power lane along the back edge, 50 mm or more behind the data lane, and reaches its radio through the row gap and the aisles, away from the data cables. Bend radius 5 x the cable diameter or more; Velcro every 300 mm.

steps.title: Cable: PoE to the nodes
steps.text: 7 cables; print two ID labels per cable on the label printer and tag both ends before routing. Adaptor RJ45 to the node ETH1 at the rack rear, down the LEFT side with the power cables (seen from the front). WARNING: Q cables carry 48 V DC on an ordinary RJ45 (passive PoE, power only): never plug one into a switch, PC or laptop; put a yellow '48 V PoE - NOT ETHERNET' flag next to the ID label at both ends. Velcro to the lacing bars every 300 mm, no zip ties; Cat6A bend radius 4 x diameter (about 30 mm) or more; coil slack on the lacing bar, never at the connector.

steps.title: Cable: AC mains
steps.text: 30 cables; print two ID labels per cable on the label printer and tag both ends before routing. Fit the lead at the device inlet and at its PDU outlet (or strip outlet) only. Do NOT plug the PDU cords or the strip cord into the wall: they stay unplugged until power-up (guide section 6), and every PDU outlet stays OFF. Rack mains runs go up the LEFT side of the rack as seen from the front, 50 mm or more from coax and data, Velcroed to the rear lacing bars. The strip cord runs from its wall socket along the floor under the cable protector to the rack-side table leg, up the leg at the back edge and along the power lane to the strip inlet.

steps.title: Cable: Data to SW-DATA
steps.text: 19 cables; print two ID labels per cable on the label printer and tag both ends before routing. Data runs up the RIGHT side of the rack as seen from the front (your left-hand side at the rear). Node SFP+ (rear) to SW-DATA (front): cross from the rear to the front on the right side at SW-DATA's U. Runs to the bench table leave the rack on the right at about 560 mm behind the front rail and cross in the FRONT (data) compartment of the cable bridge (CABLE-BRIDGE) into the table's data lane, 50 mm or more in front of the power lane. Clean every LC end with the one-click cleaner before mating. Bend radius: OM4 30 mm or more, DAC 50 mm or more, Cat6A 4 x diameter. Coil slack behind the cable manager, Velcro only.

steps.title: Cable: Management to SW-OOB
steps.text: 22 cables; print two ID labels per cable on the label printer and tag both ends before routing. Management runs up the RIGHT side as seen from the front. SW-OOB and the PDUs sit on the rear posts, so their runs stay at the rear; the attenuator LAN ports are at the back of each box; BENCH-CTL, MWATT and the analyser come from the table's data lane through the front (data) compartment of the cable bridge and up the right side. Cat6A bend radius 4 x diameter; Velcro every 300 mm; slack on the lacing bars.

steps.title: Cable: GNSS
steps.text: 10 cables; print two ID labels per cable on the label printer and tag both ends before routing. First the arrestor: fit GNSS-ARR on the wall where the antenna lead enters the room, just above the lab earth bar, and bond its ground lug to the lab earth bar with B003 (6 mm2 green/yellow, short and straight, no loops; ring lugs crimped and torqued) BEFORE the antenna lead is connected to anything; if the building already has an entry arrestor, bond to that instead (facilities). Then the antenna lead G001 to the arrestor's antenna side, and the jumper G009 from its equipment side up the wall and in along the rack's LEFT side (outside the rails) to GNSS-SPL's input at the rear of the rack top. Jumpers down the RIGHT side of the rack, just outside the rails about 450 mm behind the front rail (not the rear post), then in behind each Spider box to its node's GNSS SMA. Fit an ANNE-50+ load on every unused splitter output (GNSS-SPL.out8). RG-316 bend radius 25 mm or more, LMR-400 / LMR-240 per their data sheets. Torque the SMA joints to 8 in-lb (0.9 N m) with the SMA torque wrench, holding the jack with the backing wrench.

steps.title: IF link THA (ATT-01)
steps.text: tile i of H.N to ATT-01 CH i IN; ATT-01 CH i OUT to CPL-AS.ti THRU; IN to tile i of A.S. Route every cable through the left side lane: straight out from the port, down to the lower edge of its unit (for a Spider box: on the seam with the unit below, between the two tile rows), along that edge to the side of the rack, along the side, and in along the lower edge of the other unit; never across the face of another box, so every tile keeps 16 mm or more clear above and below its SMA and the runs pass 15 mm or more in front of it. Connect the lowest tile first; torque every SMA to 8 in-lb (0.9 N m) with the SMA torque wrench while holding the jack with the backing wrench. Where a seam bundle from an earlier step lies close to a tile, ease it aside by hand and fit the torque wrench with its handle sideways; never lever against a fitted cable. The four tile cables are one stock length (equal length, not a phase-matched set: see the assumptions); coil slack in the side lane.

steps.title: Coupling arm KBD (ATT-09)
steps.text: CPL port (top) of CPL-BE.ti -> BLK-18-S+ DC block -> BW-S15W2+ 15 dB pad -> cable -> ATT-09 CH i IN; ATT-09 CH i OUT -> cable -> BLK-18-S+ DC block -> CPL port (top) of CPL-DW.ti. First screw the DC blocks and pads onto the CPL ports (ARM-BE.t1 to ARM-DW.t4: 52 mm stacks on the input side, 30 mm blocks on the output side) and torque every SMA to 8 in-lb (0.9 N m) with the SMA torque wrench while holding the jack with the backing wrench. Each cable's plug goes on top of its stack; the cable bends level 95 mm above the CPL port, moves to its row's lane to the right of the stack, leaves forward over the tray front and runs through the side lane as in the link steps. The four arm cables of each side are one stock length (equal length, not a phase-matched set). Pad value from the arm budget (assumptions): attenuator about 11.5 dB at INR 13 dB.

steps.title: IP-50 conducted chains
steps.text: Radio -> waveguide transition (bolted to the radio flange) -> SA18S10W-30 30 dB pad -> SMA cable (0.61-1.22 m, see the table) -> MWATT CH j IN; CH j OUT -> SMA cable -> pad -> transition -> radio. The SMA cables drop from the transition to the table top and run on it, round MWATT's front corner, to its front ports. Torque every SMA to 8 in-lb (0.9 N m) with the SMA torque wrench while holding the jack with the backing wrench. The radios stay unpowered until the last stage of power-up, after every chain is closed and every MWATT channel is set.

steps.title: Checks and power-up
steps.text: Run the install checks (guide section 6). Before mains: every earth bond fitted and checked under 0.1 ohm (B001-B010), the GNSS arrestor bonded (B003) before its lead is on the splitter; every PDU outlet OFF with power-on state OFF (set when the PDUs were commissioned), every DC breaker OFF (the DCD1M main breaker too), every GMT fuse out, every DC load end unlanded and taped, the strip switch OFF. Then power up: PDUs (cords into WALL.S1-S2 and check every outlet reads OFF), switches and bench controller (strip cord into WALL.S3 and strip ON; switch the SW-DATA / SW-OOB / GNSS-SPL outlets ON at the front panel; wait for them to boot), attenuators (their outlets ON; BENCH-CTL sets every attenuator and MWATT channel to its start value), servers and hosts (outlets ON; SRV-E2E first), DC rectifiers (earth bonds checked; outlets ON; meter each breaker / fuse output at its free load end before landing the load), nodes (close CB8-CB10 (box fans) first and check every fan runs; then CB1-CB7 one at a time), radios last (GMT fuses F1-F6 in one at a time; only after every chain is closed and every MWATT channel is set).

power_up.title: DC rectifiers
power_up.do: earth bonds checked; outlets ON; meter each breaker / fuse output at its free load end before landing the load
power_up.detail: with the rectifiers still off, check every earth bond end to end with the meter on ohms (leads nulled), under 0.1 ohm (B001-B010); with both rectifiers off, every CB open and every GMT fuse out, meter ohms: DC-DIST + bus to DC-DIST return, + bus to RACK-EARTH and return to RACK-EARTH; DC-DIST2 bus A and bus B to RTN: each must climb to OL or above 1 Mohm (the rectifier capacitors charge first); a reading under 1 kohm is a short or an earth fault (reversed strap, nicked run): find it before switching on; DC-DIST2 RTN to RACK-EARTH must read under 0.1 ohm (positive-ground system); the +48 V system stays floating: do not bond it to earth; switch ON PDU-A.O1 (DC-RECT module 1), PDU-B.O11 (DC-RECT module 2), PDU-A.O2 (DC-RECT2); close the DCD1M main / input breaker if fitted, with every CB still open, and meter the DC-DIST bus: + bus to return +43 to +56 V; then check the earth reference with COM on RACK-EARTH: DC-DIST2 RTN reads 0 V and DC-DIST2 bus A reads -43 to -56 V; then one position at a time (CB1-CB10 and F1-F6): close the breaker (or insert the fuse), meter COM on the return (unsleeved) conductor and the red probe on the supply (sleeved) conductor at the free load end: a DC-DIST breaker output reads about +48 V (+43 to +56 V); a DC-DIST2 fuse output reads about -48 V (-43 to -56 V); any other sign or value: stop, open the breaker or pull the fuse and correct the run at its supply end; open the breaker (pull the fuse with the fuse puller) again, then land the red / blue-sleeved conductor on the load's + terminal (PA adaptor, Spider DCIN) or -48 V pin (radio) and the unsleeved conductor on the other, torque adaptor and DCIN terminals to the value marked on them, and for a radio mate the DC connector; CB10 carries 2 runs (D019, D020): meter every free end before landing any

power_up.title: nodes
power_up.do: close CB8-CB10 (box fans) first and check every fan runs; then CB1-CB7 one at a time
power_up.detail: close DC-DIST CB8 (SB1 DCIN), CB9 (SB2 DCIN), CB10 (SB3 + SB4 DCIN) one at a time and check that each box's fans run within 1 min (if not: open that breaker, leave the nodes of every box it feeds off and find out why); then close DC-DIST CB1 (PA-01, node B), CB2 (PA-02, node E), CB3 (PA-03, node H), CB4 (PA-04, node A), CB5 (PA-05, node D), CB6 (PA-06, node C), CB7 (PA-07, node F) one at a time; if a box's fans stop while its nodes boot, power that box down: SB1: CB1, CB2, then CB8; SB2: CB3, then CB9; SB3 or SB4: CB4, CB5, CB6, CB7, then CB10 (CB10 feeds the fans of SB3 and SB4); wait for every node to join the E2E controller; then read each PDU's input current on its own display (PDU-A, PDU-B): each must be 12.8 A or less (80 % of 16 A); if one is above, stop and move a load (PDU-B is within 10 % of its limit on the estimates: read it first)

power_up.title: radios last
power_up.do: GMT fuses F1-F6 in one at a time; only after every chain is closed and every MWATT channel is set
power_up.detail: first confirm every IP-50 chain (W001-W012) is complete and torqued (transition bolted, pad and cable on, no open flange or SMA) and MWATT reads back its start value on every channel; never power a radio with an open RF port; then insert the GMT fuses on DC-DIST2 one at a time: F1 (IP50-MAF@A), F2 (IP50-MAF@F), F3 (IP50-MBE@B), F4 (IP50-MBE@E), F5 (IP50-MCD@C), F6 (IP50-MCD@D); after 30 min check every radio's temperature (the stacked ones in particular) in the IP-50 web UI or CLI, reached in-band over the data network from SRV-E2E (the NMS host; BENCH-CTL has no data-network port); then read each PDU's input current on its own display (PDU-A, PDU-B): each must be 12.8 A or less (80 % of 16 A); if one is above, stop and move a load
